value.zh: 幷人以為怯，競攀堞而登，晏麾伏兵擊之，顛死者甚眾，遂焚橋遁。
value.en: The Bing troops thought him cowardly and swarmed the battlements. Yan signaled his ambush, and many fell to their deaths. He then burned the bridge and withdrew.
value.literal: The Bing men thought him cowardly and scrambled up the battlements to climb; Yan waved his hidden troops to strike them, and very many fell headlong to their deaths. He then burned the bridge and fled.

value.zh: 遣漢倫追北數十里，斬首百餘級，擢漢倫濱州刺史。
value.en: He sent Hanlun in pursuit for dozens of li, took more than a hundred heads, and promoted Hanlun to prefect of Binzhou.
value.literal: He sent Hanlun in pursuit north for several tens of li, beheaded more than a hundred heads, and promoted Hanlun to prefect of Binzhou.

value.zh: 八月來朝，周祖以晏家彭城，授武寧軍節度，俾榮其鄉里。
value.en: He came to court in the eighth month. Because Yan's family came from Pengcheng, the Zhou founder made him military governor of Wuning so his homeland might share in the honor.
value.literal: In the eighth month he came to court; because Yan's family was from Pengcheng, the Zhou founder appointed him military governor of the Wuning army so that his home district might be honored.

value.zh: 三年，周祖征兗州，次張康鎮，晏來朝，獻馬七匹，賜襲衣、金帶。
value.en: In the third year, while the Zhou founder campaigned against Yanzhou and halted at Zhangkang, Yan came to court with seven horses and received ceremonial robes and a gold belt.
value.literal: In the third year, as the Zhou founder campaigned against Yanzhou and halted at Zhangkang town, Yan came to court, presented seven horses, and was granted ceremonial robes and a gold belt.

value.zh: 親郊畢，封滕國公，加開府階。
value.en: After the suburban sacrifice he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng and given Ministerial rank.
value.literal: When the suburban sacrifice was completed, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng and given Ministerial rank.

value.zh: 世宗即位，加兼中書令。
value.en: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Yan was made concurrent Chief Secretary.
value.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Yan] was given the additional title of concurrent Chief Secretary.

value.zh: 顯德初，加開府階，進封譙國公。
value.en: Early in Xiande he received Ministerial rank and was advanced to Duke of Qiao.
value.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was given Ministerial rank and advanced to Duke of Qiao.

value.zh: 世宗即位，兼中書令。
value.en: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Xingde was made concurrent Chief Secretary.
value.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Xingde] was made concurrent Chief Secretary.

value.zh: 初，世宗處河東還，次河陽，以洛陽城頭缺，令葺之。
value.en: When Emperor Shizong had settled Hedong and was returning, he halted at Heyang. Finding Luoyang's battlements in disrepair, he ordered them restored.
value.literal: At first, when Emperor Shizong had settled Hedong and was returning, he halted at Heyang. Because the battlements of Luoyang were deficient, he ordered them repaired.

value.zh: 行德率部民萬餘完其城，封邢國公。
value.en: Xingde led more than ten thousand local people to complete the walls and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.
value.literal: Xingde led more than ten thousand local people to complete the city and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.

value.zh: 是秋，代王晏為武寧軍節度，與晏兩換其任。
value.en: That autumn he and Wang Yan exchanged posts, Xingde taking the Wuning governorship.
value.literal: That autumn he replaced Wang Yan as military governor of the Wuning army, the two exchanging their posts.

value.zh: 先是，唐末楊氏據淮甸，自甬橋東南決汴，匯為汙澤。
value.en: Earlier, late in Tang the Yang clan held the Huai region. Southeast of Yongqiao they breached the Bian River, turning it into a foul marsh.
value.literal: Earlier, late in Tang the Yang clan held the Huai region; from Yongqiao southeast they breached the Bian River, which pooled into a foul marsh.

value.zh: 二年，將議南征，遣行德率所部丁壯於古堤疏導之，東達於泗上。
value.en: In the second year, as a southern campaign was planned, Xingde was sent to lead his able-bodied men in dredging the old embankment east to the Si River.
value.literal: In the second year, as a southern campaign was being planned, [the court] sent Xingde to lead the able-bodied men of his command in dredging and channeling it along the old embankment east as far as the Si River.

value.zh: 及親征，以行德為濠州行營都部署，破淮軍二千餘人於郡境。
value.en: On the personal campaign, Xingde was made overall commander at Haozhou and defeated more than two thousand Huai troops in the prefecture.
value.literal: When the emperor campaigned in person, Xingde was made overall commander of the Haozhou field headquarters and defeated more than two thousand Huai troops within the prefecture.

value.zh: 俄遣率師屯定遠以逼其城，為吳所敗，死者數百人，行德以身免，左授右衛上將軍。
value.en: Soon he led troops to garrison Dingyuan and press the city, but Wu defeated him and several hundred died. Xingde escaped alive and was demoted to Grand General of the Right Guard.
value.literal: Soon he was sent to lead troops garrisoned at Dingyuan to press the city; he was defeated by Wu, several hundred died, and Xingde escaped with his life. He was demoted and appointed Grand General of the Right Guard.

value.zh: 五年，下淮南，復授行德保大軍節度兼中書令。
value.en: In the fifth year, after Huainan fell, Xingde was again made military governor of Baoda and concurrent Chief Secretary.
value.literal: In the fifth year Huainan was taken; Xingde was again appointed military governor of the Baoda army and concurrent Chief Secretary.

value.zh: 恭帝嗣位，進封宋國公。
value.en: When Emperor Gongdi succeeded to the throne, Xingde was advanced to Duke of Song.
value.literal: When Emperor Gongdi succeeded to the throne, [Xingde] was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Song.

value.zh: 王肅 宋弁
value.en: Wang Su; Song Bian
value.literal: Wang Su; Song Bian

value.zh: 誦，字國章，肅長兄融之子。
value.en: Song, whose courtesy name was Guozhang, was the son of Su's elder brother Rong.
value.literal: Song, styled Guozhang, was the son of Su's elder brother Rong.

value.zh: 學涉有文才，神氣清儁，風流甚美。
value.en: He was learned and gifted in letters, with a clear and handsome presence and an exceptionally refined bearing.
value.literal: He studied broadly and had literary talent; his spirit was clear and handsome, and his bearing exceedingly fine.

value.zh: 自員外郎、司徒主簿，轉司徒屬、司空諮議、通直常侍、汝南王友。
value.en: He rose from Gentleman of the Palace and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education to Attendant of the Minister of Education, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Direct Regular Attendant, and Companion to the Prince of Runan.
value.literal: From Gentleman of the Palace, Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, he was transferred to Attendant of the Minister of Education, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Direct Regular Attendant, and Companion to the Prince of Runan.

value.zh: 遷司徒諮議，加前軍、散騎常侍、光祿大夫。
value.en: He was promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, with additional titles of Vanguard General, Attendant at the Palace Cadet, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
value.literal: He was promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, with additional titles of Vanguard General, Attendant at the Palace Cadet, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

value.zh: 出為左將軍、幽州刺史。
value.en: He was sent out as General of the Left and Inspector of You Province.
value.literal: He was sent out as General of the Left and Inspector of You Province.

value.zh: 未幾，徵為長兼祕書監，徙給事黃門侍郎。
value.en: Before long he was recalled as Senior Acting Director of the Palace Library, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
value.literal: Before long he was summoned as Senior Acting Director of the Palace Library, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

value.zh: 肅宗崩，靈太后之立幼主也，於時大赦，誦宣讀詔書，音制抑揚，風神疎秀，百僚傾屬，莫不歎美。
value.en: When Emperor Suzong died and Empress Dowager Ling installed the young emperor, a general amnesty was proclaimed. Song read the edict aloud with cadences rising and falling, his bearing open and refined. The officials all turned to him in admiration.
value.literal: When Suzong died and Empress Dowager Ling established the young ruler, there was at the time a great amnesty; Song read the edict aloud, his tones rising and falling, his bearing open and refined; the hundred officials turned to him, and none failed to sigh in admiration.

value.zh: 孝莊初，於河陰遇害，年三十七。
value.en: Early in the Xiaozhuang reign he was killed at Heyin, at the age of thirty-seven.
value.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang, he met with violence at Heyin, aged thirty-seven.

value.zh: [3]贈驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、司空公、徐州刺史，諡曰文宣。
value.en: [3] He was posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Wenhuan.
value.literal: [3] Posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title Wenhuan.

value.zh: 誦弟衍，字文舒。
value.en: Song's younger brother Yan, whose courtesy name was Wenshu.
value.literal: Song's younger brother Yan, styled Wenshu.

value.zh: 名行器藝亞於誦。
value.en: His reputation, conduct, and abilities were second only to Song's.
value.literal: His reputation, conduct, talent, and skill were second to Song's.

value.zh: 自著作佐郎，稍遷尚書郎、員外常侍、司空諮議、光祿大夫、廷尉、揚州大中正、度支尚書，仍轉七兵，徙太常卿。
value.en: Starting as Assistant Gentleman of the Academy, he rose through Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat, Acting Regular Attendant, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Justice, Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, and Director of Revenue, then transferred to the Seven Troops and became Minister of Ceremonies.
value.literal: From Assistant Gentleman of the Academy he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat, Acting Regular Attendant, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Justice, Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, Director of Revenue, then transferred to the Seven Troops, and moved to Minister of Ceremonies.

value.zh: 出為散騎常侍、征東將軍、西兗州刺史。
value.en: He was sent out as Attendant at the Palace Cadet, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Western Yanzhou.
value.literal: He was sent out as Attendant at the Palace Cadet, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Western Yanzhou.

value.zh: 衍屆治未幾，屬尒朱仲遠稱兵內向，州既路衝，為其攻逼。
value.en: Yan had been in office only a short time when Erzhu Zhongyuan raised troops and marched inward. The province lay on the main route and came under his attack.
value.literal: Yan had been in office only a short time when Erzhu Zhongyuan raised troops and marched inward; the province being on the main route, he was attacked and pressed by him.

value.zh: 衍不能守，為仲遠所擒，以其名望不害也，令其騎牛從軍，久乃見釋。
value.en: Yan could not hold the province and was captured by Zhongyuan. Because of his reputation he was not harmed, but was made to ride an ox with the army. Only after a long time was he released.
value.literal: Yan could not hold it and was captured by Zhongyuan; because of his reputation he was not harmed, but was made to ride an ox with the army; only after a long time was he released.

value.zh: 還洛，除車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。
value.en: On returning to Luoyang he was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
value.literal: Returning to Luoyang, he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

value.zh: 孝靜初，轉侍中，將軍如故。
value.en: Early in the Xiaojing reign he was made Palace Attendant while retaining his general's title.
value.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing, he was transferred to Palace Attendant; his general's title as before.

value.zh: 天平三年卒，年五十二。
value.en: In the third year of the Tianping reign he died, at the age of fifty-two.
value.literal: In the third year of Tianping he died, aged fifty-two.

value.zh: 敕給東園祕器、賵物三百段，贈使持節、都督青徐兗三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、徐州刺史，諡曰文獻。
value.en: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and three hundred sections of funeral goods. He was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Wenxian.
value.literal: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and three hundred sections of funeral goods; posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Qing, Xu, and Yan, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title Wenxian.

value.zh: 衍篤於交舊，有故人竺虩，於西兗為仲遠所害，其妻子飢寒，衍置之於家，累年贍恤，世人稱其敦厚。
value.en: Yan was devoted to old friends. An acquaintance named Zhu Xi had been killed by Zhongyuan in Western Yanzhou, leaving his wife and children hungry and cold. Yan took them into his household and supported them for years, and the world praised his generosity.
value.literal: Yan was devoted to old friends; he had an old acquaintance Zhu Xi who was killed by Zhongyuan in Western Yanzhou; his wife and children were hungry and cold; Yan took them into his household and for years provided support; the world praised his generosity.

value.zh: 袁躍 裴敬憲 盧觀 封肅 邢臧 裴伯茂 邢昕 溫子昇
value.en: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, and Wen Zisheng
value.literal: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, Wen Zisheng

value.zh: 正光末，廣陽王淵為東北道行臺，召為郎中，軍國文翰皆出其手。
value.en: At the end of Zhengguang, Prince Yuan of Guangyang served as Northeast Circuit Commander and summoned Zisheng as Gentleman; all military and state papers came from his hand.
value.literal: At the end of Zhengguang, Prince Yuan of Guangyang served as Northeast Circuit Commander; he summoned Zisheng as Gentleman; all military and state documents issued from his hand.

value.zh: 於是才名轉盛。
value.en: His fame for talent then grew still greater.
value.literal: Thereupon his fame for talent grew still greater.

value.zh: 黃門郎徐紇受四方表啟，答之敏速，於淵獨沉思曰：「彼有溫郎中，才藻可畏。」
value.en: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu Hong received memorials from the four quarters and answered them swiftly; facing Yuan alone he mused and said, "They have Gentleman Wen on staff—his literary power inspires dread."
value.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu Hong received memorials from the four directions and answered swiftly; facing Yuan alone he pondered and said: "They have Gentleman Wen there—his literary talent is formidable."

value.zh: 高車破走，珍實盈滿，子昇取絹四十匹。
value.en: When the Gaoche were routed, booty filled the tents; Zisheng took forty bolts of silk.
value.literal: When the Gaoche were routed and fled, treasures filled the camp; Zisheng took forty bolts of silk.

value.zh: 及淵為葛榮所害，子昇亦見羈執。
value.en: When Yuan was slain by Ge Rong, Zisheng too was seized and detained.
value.literal: When Yuan was killed by Ge Rong, Zisheng was also seized and held.

value.zh: 榮下都督和洛興與子昇舊識，以數十騎潛送子昇，得達冀州。
value.en: Heluo Xing, a subordinate commander under Rong and an old acquaintance of Zisheng, secretly escorted him with several dozen horsemen until he reached Jizhou.
value.literal: Ge Rong's subordinate commander Heluo Xing was an old acquaintance of Zisheng; with several dozen horsemen he secretly sent Zisheng off, enabling him to reach Jizhou.

value.zh: 還京，李楷執其手曰：「卿今得免，足使夷甫慚德。」
value.en: On returning to the capital, Li Kai grasped his hand and said, "You have come through alive—enough to make Yifu blush for his character."
value.literal: Returning to the capital, Li Kai took his hand and said: "You have now escaped—enough to make Yifu ashamed of his virtue."

value.zh: 自是無復宦情，閉門讀書，厲精不已。
value.en: From then on he lost all desire for office, shut his door to read, and honed his mind without cease.
value.literal: From then on he had no further desire for office, shut his door and read books, and refined his mind without cease.

value.zh: 郭崇韜
value.en: Guo Chongtao
value.literal: Guo Chongtao

value.zh: 明年征蜀，議擇大將。
value.en: The next year they marched against Shu and debated who should lead.
value.literal: The next year they marched against Shu and debated choosing a chief general.

value.zh: 時明宗為總管，當行。
value.en: Mingzong was then overall commander and was the man who ought to go.
value.literal: At that time Mingzong was overall commander and ought to go.

value.zh: 而崇韜以讒見危，思立大功為自安之計，乃曰：「契丹為患北邊，非總管不可禦。
value.en: Chongtao, endangered by slander, sought a great victory to save himself and said: “The Khitan threaten the north—only the overall commander can hold them.
value.literal: But Chongtao, endangered by slander, thought to secure himself with a great feat and said: “The Khitan trouble the northern frontier; only the overall commander can repel them.

value.zh: 魏王繼岌，國之儲副，而大功未立，且親王為元帥，唐故事也。」
value.en: Prince Jiji is the heir, yet he has won no great deed; and an imperial prince as field marshal is Tang custom.”
value.literal: Prince Jiji is the heir, yet he has won no great merit; moreover, an imperial prince as commander-in-chief is Tang custom.”

value.zh: 莊宗曰：「繼岌，小子，豈任大事？
value.en: Zhuangzong said: “Jiji is a boy—can he bear so great a burden?
value.literal: Zhuangzong said: “Jiji is a boy—can he bear so great a charge?

value.zh: 必為我擇其副。」
value.en: Choose his deputy for me.”
value.literal: You must choose his deputy for me.”

value.zh: 崇韜未及言，莊宗曰：「吾得之矣，無以易卿也。」
value.en: Before Chongtao could answer, Zhuangzong said: “I have my man—none can replace you.”
value.literal: Before Chongtao could speak, Zhuangzong said: “I have my man—none can replace you.”

value.zh: 乃以繼岌為西南面行營都統，崇韜為招討使，軍政皆決崇韜。
value.en: He made Jiji overall commander for the southwest campaign and Chongtao pacification commissioner; military and civil affairs alike rested with Chongtao.
value.literal: He then made Jiji overall commander for the southwest campaign and Chongtao pacification commissioner; all military and political decisions rested with Chongtao.

value.zh: 唐軍入蜀，所過迎降。
value.en: Tang troops entered Shu; wherever they marched, cities came out to surrender.
value.literal: Tang troops entered Shu; wherever they passed, cities surrendered in welcome.

value.zh: 王衍弟宗弼，陰送款於崇韜，求為西川兵馬留後，崇韜以節度使許之。
value.en: Wang Yan’s brother Zongbi secretly sent terms to Chongtao, asking to be kept on as Xichuan military commissioner; Chongtao promised him the circuit.
value.literal: Wang Yan’s brother Zongbi secretly sent terms to Chongtao, asking to be kept-on military commissioner of Xichuan; Chongtao promised him the governorship.

value.zh: 軍至成都，宗弼遷衍於西宮，悉取衍嬪妓、珍寶奉崇韜及其子廷誨。
value.en: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and sent Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to Chongtao and his son Tinghui.
value.literal: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and gathered Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to present to Chongtao and his son Tinghui.

value.zh: 又與蜀人列狀見魏王，請崇韜留鎮蜀。
value.en: Shu men also petitioned the Prince of Wei to keep Chongtao in command of Shu.
value.literal: Shu men also filed a petition to the Prince of Wei asking Chongtao to remain and govern Shu.

value.zh: 繼岌頗疑崇韜，崇韜無以自明，因以事斬宗弼及其弟宗渥、宗勛，沒其家財。
value.en: Jiji grew deeply suspicious of Chongtao. Unable to clear himself, Chongtao seized on a pretext to execute Zongbi and his brothers Zongwo and Zongxun and confiscate their property.
value.literal: Jiji grew quite suspicious of Chongtao; Chongtao could not clear himself and therefore had Zongbi and his brothers Zongwo and Zongxun executed and their property confiscated.

value.zh: 蜀人大恐。
value.en: The people of Shu were terrified.
value.literal: The people of Shu were greatly terrified.

value.zh: 王建，字光圖，許州舞陽人也。
value.en: Wang Jian, whose courtesy name was Guangtu, came from Wuyang in Xuzhou.
value.literal: Wang Jian, courtesy name Guangtu, was a native of Wuyang in Xuzhou.

value.zh: 隆眉廣顙，狀貌偉然。
value.en: He had heavy brows and a broad forehead, and his bearing was imposing.
value.literal: Heavy brows and a broad forehead, his appearance imposing.

value.zh: 少無賴，以屠牛、盜驢、販私鹽為事，里人謂之「賊王八」。
value.en: As a young man he was a rascal who made his living slaughtering oxen, stealing donkeys, and smuggling salt; neighbors called him "Bandit Wang Eight."
value.literal: In youth he was a rascal, making his living slaughtering oxen, stealing donkeys, and trafficking in illicit salt; the neighborhood called him "Bandit Wang Eight."

value.zh: 後為忠武軍卒，稍遷隊將。
value.en: He later enlisted in the Zhongwu Army and gradually rose to company commander.
value.literal: Later he became a soldier of the Zhongwu Army and gradually rose to company commander.

value.zh: 衍字化源。
value.en: Yan, whose courtesy name was Huayuan.
value.literal: Yan, courtesy name Huayuan.

value.zh: 建十一子，曰衛王宗仁，簡王元膺，趙王宗紀，豳王宗輅，韓王宗智，莒王宗特，信王宗傑，魯王宗鼎，興王宗澤，薛王宗平。
value.en: Jian had eleven sons: the Princes of Wei Zongren, Jian Yuanying, Zhao Zongji, Bin Zonglu, Han Zongzhi, Ju Zongte, Xin Zongjie, Lu Zongding, Xing Zongze, and Xue Zongping.
value.literal: Jian had eleven sons: Prince of Wei Zongren, Prince of Jian Yuanying, Prince of Zhao Zongji, Prince of Bin Zonglu, Prince of Han Zongzhi, Prince of Ju Zongte, Prince of Xin Zongjie, Prince of Lu Zongding, Prince of Xing Zongze, and Prince of Xue Zongping.

value.zh: 而鄭王宗衍最幼，其母徐賢妃也，以母寵得立為皇太子，開崇賢府，置官屬，後更曰天策府。
value.en: The Prince of Zheng, Zongyan, was the youngest. His mother was Consort Xu the Worthy. Favored through her influence, he was made crown prince, opened the Chongxian bureau and appointed its staff, later renamed the Tiance bureau.
value.literal: Prince of Zheng Zongyan was the youngest; his mother was Consort Xu the Worthy. Through his mother's favor he was established as crown prince, opened the Chongxian Bureau and appointed officials, later renamed the Tiance Bureau.

value.zh: 衍為人方頤大口，垂手過膝，顧目見耳，頗知學問，能為浮艷之辭。
value.en: Yan had a square face and large mouth, hands that hung past his knees, and eyes so prominent that they could be seen from behind; he was fairly learned and could write florid verse.
value.literal: Yan had a square face and large mouth, hands hanging past his knees, and when he turned his head his eyes could be seen from behind; he was fairly learned and could compose florid verses.

value.zh: 元膺死，建以豳王宗輅貌類己，而信王宗傑於諸子最材賢，欲於兩人擇立之。
value.en: After Yuanying died, Jian thought Prince Zonglu of Bin resembled him in looks and Prince Zongjie of Xin was the most talented of his sons, and he meant to choose between them.
value.literal: After Yuanying's death Jian considered that Prince of Bin Zonglu resembled him in appearance, while Prince of Xin Zongjie was the most talented and worthy among his sons, and wished to choose between the two to install.

value.zh: 而徐妃專寵，建老昏耄，妃與宦者唐文扆教相者上言衍相最貴，又諷宰相張格贊成之，衍由是得為太子。
value.en: But Consort Xu held exclusive favor, and the aging Jian was senile. She and the eunuch Tang Wenyi coached physiognomists to declare Yan's face the most exalted and urged chief minister Zhang Ge to endorse it, and Yan became crown prince.
value.literal: But Consort Xu held exclusive favor; Jian in his old age was senile. The consort and the eunuch Tang Wenyi instructed physiognomists to report that Yan's physiognomy was the most exalted, and also prompted Chief Minister Zhang Ge to endorse it; Yan thereby became crown prince.

value.zh: 建卒，衍立，謚建曰神武聖文孝德明惠皇帝，廟號高祖，陵曰永陵。
value.en: When Jian died, Yan succeeded him, posthumously titling him Emperor Shenwu Shengwen Xiaode Minghui, with temple name Gaozu and tomb Yongling.
value.literal: When Jian died Yan succeeded him, posthumously titling Jian Emperor Shenwu Shengwen Xiaode Minghui, temple name Gaozu, tomb Yongling.

value.zh: 建正室周氏號昭聖皇后，後建數日而卒，衍因尊其母徐氏為皇太后，後妹淑妃為皇太妃。
value.en: Jian's principal consort, Lady Zhou, was titled Empress Zhaosheng and died a few days after him. Yan therefore honored his mother Lady Xu as empress dowager and his younger sister the Pure Consort as grand imperial consort.
value.literal: Jian's principal consort Lady Zhou was titled Empress Zhaosheng; she died a few days after Jian. Yan therefore honored his mother Lady Xu as empress dowager and his younger sister the Pure Consort as grand imperial consort.

value.zh: 太后、太妃以教令賣官，自刺史以下，每一官闕，必數人並爭，而入錢多者得之；
value.en: The empress dowager and grand imperial consort sold offices by edict. From prefect downward, every vacancy drew several bidders, and the highest payment won;
value.literal: The empress dowager and grand imperial consort sold offices by edict; from prefect downward, for every vacancy several men would compete, and whoever paid the most obtained it;

value.zh: 通都大邑起邸店，以奪民利。
value.en: and in major cities they opened government shops to seize profits from the people.
value.literal: in major cities they set up government shops to seize the people's profits.

value.zh: 衍年少荒淫，委其政於宦者宋光嗣、光葆、景潤澄、王承休、歐陽晃、田魯儔等；
value.en: Yan in his youth was dissolute and entrusted government to the eunuchs Song Guangsi, Guangbao, Jing Runcheng, Wang Chengxiu, Ouyang Huang, Tian Luchou, and others;
value.literal: Yan in his youth was dissolute and entrusted government to the eunuchs Song Guangsi, Guangbao, Jing Runcheng, Wang Chengxiu, Ouyang Huang, Tian Luchou, and others;

value.zh: 以韓昭、潘在迎、顧在珣、嚴旭等為狎客；
value.en: he took Han Zhao, Pan Zaiying, Gu Zaixun, Yan Xu, and others as intimate companions;
value.literal: he made Han Zhao, Pan Zaiying, Gu Zaixun, Yan Xu, and others his intimate companions;

value.zh: 起宣華苑，有重光、太清、延昌、會真之殿，清和、迎仙之宮，降真、蓬萊、丹霞之亭，飛鸞之閣，瑞獸之門；
value.en: he built the Xuanhua Garden with halls named Chongguang, Taiqing, Yanchang, and Huizhen, palaces named Qinghe and Yingxian, pavilions named Jiangzhen, Penglai, and Danxia, the Feiluan Pavilion, and the Ruishou Gate;
value.literal: he built the Xuanhua Garden, with halls of Chongguang, Taiqing, Yanchang, and Huizhen, palaces of Qinghe and Yingxian, pavilions of Jiangzhen, Penglai, and Danxia, the Feiluan Pavilion, and the Ruishou Gate;

value.zh: 又作怡神亭，與諸狎客、婦人日夜酣飲其中。
value.en: he also built the Yishen Pavilion, where he drank day and night with his companions and women.
value.literal: he also built the Yishen Pavilion and with his intimate companions and women drank deep day and night within it.

value.zh: 嘗以九日宴宣華苑，嘉王宗壽以社稷為言，言發泣涕。
value.en: Once on the Double Ninth he feasted in the Xuanhua Garden. Prince Zongshou spoke of the fate of the realm and wept as he spoke.
value.literal: Once on the Double Ninth he feasted in the Xuanhua Garden; Prince Zongshou spoke of the altars of state and wept as he spoke.

value.zh: 韓昭等曰：「嘉王酒悲爾！」
value.en: Han Zhao and the others said, "The prince is drunk and maudlin!"
value.literal: Han Zhao and the others said: "The prince is drunk and maudlin!"

value.zh: 諸狎客共以慢言謔嘲之，坐上喧然。
value.en: The companions all mocked him with disrespectful jests, and the hall erupted in laughter.
value.literal: The intimate companions all mocked him with disrespectful words, and the gathering became uproarious.

value.zh: 衍不能省也。
value.en: Yan took no notice.
value.literal: Yan could not perceive it.

value.zh: 蜀人富而喜遨，當王氏晚年，俗競為小帽，僅覆其頂，俯首即墮，謂之「危腦帽」。
value.en: The people of Shu were wealthy and fond of outings. In the Wangs' later years the fashion was for tiny caps that barely covered the crown and fell off at a bow, called "perilous-brain caps."
value.literal: The people of Shu were wealthy and fond of outings; in the late years of the Wang house the custom competed in small caps that barely covered the crown and fell off at a bow, called "perilous-brain caps."

value.zh: 衍以為不祥，禁之。
value.en: Yan took this as an ill omen and banned it.
value.literal: Yan took this as inauspicious and forbade it.

value.zh: 而衍好戴大帽，每微服出遊民間，民間以大帽識之，因令國中皆戴大帽。
value.en: Yet Yan favored large caps. When he went out in disguise, people recognized him by his large cap, so he ordered everyone in the realm to wear large caps.
value.literal: Yet Yan liked to wear large caps; whenever he went out in disguise among the people they recognized him by the large cap, and he therefore ordered the whole realm to wear large caps.

value.zh: 又好裹尖巾，其狀如錐。
value.en: He also favored pointed kerchiefs wrapped like cones.
value.literal: He also liked to wrap pointed kerchiefs shaped like cones.

value.zh: 而後宮皆戴金蓮花冠，衣道士服，酒酣免冠，其髻髽然，更施朱粉，號「醉妝」，國中之人皆效之。
value.en: The palace women wore golden lotus crowns and Daoist robes. When drunk they removed their caps, bound their hair in topknots, applied rouge, and called the look "drunken makeup," which the whole realm imitated.
value.literal: The palace women all wore golden lotus crowns and dressed in Daoist robes; when drunk they removed their caps, their hair bound in topknots, then applied rouge and powder, styling it "drunken makeup," and people throughout the realm imitated it.

value.zh: 嘗與太后、太妃遊青城山，宮人衣服，皆畫雲霞，飄然望之若仙。
value.en: Once he toured Mount Qingcheng with the empress dowager and grand imperial consort. The palace women's robes were painted with clouds and mist and seemed from afar like drifting immortals.
value.literal: Once he toured Mount Qingcheng with the empress dowager and grand imperial consort; the palace women's garments were all painted with clouds and mist, and seen from afar they seemed like immortals drifting.

value.zh: 衍自作《甘州曲》，述其仙狀，上下山谷，衍常自歌，而使宮人皆和之。
value.en: Yan composed the "Ganzhou Tune" describing their immortal aspect. As they went up and down the valleys he would sing it himself while the palace women joined in.
value.literal: Yan himself composed the "Ganzhou Tune," describing their immortal aspect; up and down the valleys Yan would often sing it himself and have the palace women all join in harmony.

value.zh: 衍立之明年，改元乾德。
value.en: The year after Yan's accession he renamed the era Qiande.
value.literal: The year after Yan's accession he changed the era name to Qiande.

value.zh: 乾德元年正月，祀天南郊，大赦，加尊號為聖德明孝皇帝。
value.en: In the first month of Qiande year 1 he sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and added the honorific Emperor Shengde Mingxiao.
value.literal: In the first month of the first year of Qiande he sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and augmented his honorific to Emperor Shengde Mingxiao.

value.zh: 二年冬，北巡，至於西縣，旌旗戈甲，連亙百餘里。
value.en: In the winter of year 2 he toured north as far as Xixian, with banners, flags, weapons, and armor stretching more than a hundred li.
value.literal: In the winter of the second year he toured north as far as Xixian; banners, flags, weapons, and armor stretched in an unbroken line for more than a hundred li.

value.zh: 其還也，自閬州浮江而上，龍舟畫舸，昭耀江水，所在供億，人不堪命。
value.en: On his return he went upriver from Lang Prefecture in dragon boats and painted barges that dazzled the waters. Every district along the route was levied beyond endurance.
value.literal: On his return he went upriver by boat from Lang Prefecture; dragon boats and painted barges dazzled the river, and wherever he passed the levies of supplies were more than men could bear.

value.zh: 三年正月，還成都。
value.en: In the first month of year 3 he returned to Chengdu.
value.literal: In the first month of the third year he returned to Chengdu.

value.zh: 五年，起上清宮，塑王子晉像，尊以為聖祖至道玉宸皇帝，又塑建及衍像，侍立於其左右；
value.en: In year 5 he built the Shangqing Palace, molded an image of Prince Zijin and honored him as the Holy Ancestor Emperor Yuchen of the Supreme Way, and molded images of Jian and Yan standing in attendance at his sides;
value.literal: In the fifth year he built the Shangqing Palace, molded an image of Prince Zijin and honored him as the Holy Ancestor Emperor Yuchen of the Supreme Way, and also molded images of Jian and Yan standing in attendance at his left and right;

value.zh: 又於正殿塑玄元皇帝及唐諸帝，備法駕而朝之。
value.en: in the main hall he also molded the Mysterious Origin Emperor and the Tang emperors, arrayed the imperial equipage, and performed court before them.
value.literal: in the main hall he also molded the Mysterious Origin Emperor and the emperors of Tang, arrayed the imperial equipage, and performed court to them.

value.zh: 六年，以王承休為天雄節度使。
value.en: In year 6 he appointed Wang Chengxiu military commissioner of Tianxiong.
value.literal: In the sixth year he made Wang Chengxiu military commissioner of Tianxiong.

value.zh: 天雄軍，秦州也。
value.en: The Tianxiong army was stationed at Qin Prefecture.
value.literal: The Tianxiong Army was at Qin Prefecture.

value.zh: 承休以宦者得幸，為宣徽使，承休妻嚴氏，有絕色，衍通之。
value.en: Chengxiu had gained favor as a eunuch and become palace attendant. His wife Lady Yan was surpassingly beautiful, and Yan took her as a lover.
value.literal: Chengxiu as a eunuch had gained favor and become palace attendant; Chengxiu's wife Lady Yan was of surpassing beauty, and Yan had relations with her.

value.zh: 是時，唐莊宗滅梁，蜀人皆懼。
value.en: At this time Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong overthrew Liang, and the people of Shu were alarmed.
value.literal: At this time Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong extinguished Liang, and the people of Shu were all afraid.

value.zh: 莊宗遣李嚴聘蜀，衍與俱朝上清，而蜀都士庶，簾帷珠翠，夾道不絕。
value.en: Zhuangzong sent Li Yan on a friendly mission to Shu. Yan accompanied him to court at Shangqing while the capital's gentry and commoners lined the road with curtains, pearls, and jade.
value.literal: Zhuangzong sent Li Yan on a friendly mission to Shu; Yan accompanied him to court at Shangqing, while the gentry and commoners of the Shu capital with curtains, pearls, and jade lined the road without end.

value.zh: 嚴見其人物富盛，而衍驕淫，歸乃獻策伐蜀。
value.en: Yan saw a realm rich in people and goods but ruled by an arrogant, dissolute Yan, and on returning he urged an attack on Shu.
value.literal: Yan saw its people and wealth in abundance yet Yan arrogant and dissolute; on returning he submitted a plan to attack Shu.

value.zh: 明年，唐魏王繼岌、郭崇韜伐蜀。
value.en: The next year Tang's Prince of Wei Jiji and Guo Chongtao invaded Shu.
value.literal: The next year Tang's Prince of Wei Jiji and Guo Chongtao attacked Shu.

value.zh: 是歲，衍改元曰咸康。
value.en: That year Yan renamed the era Xiankang.
value.literal: That year Yan changed the era name to Xiankang.

value.zh: 衍自立，歲常獵於子來山。
value.en: Since his accession Yan had hunted yearly at Mount Zilai.
value.literal: Since Yan's accession he hunted yearly at Mount Zilai.

value.zh: 是歲，又幸彭州陽平化、漢州三學山。
value.en: That year he also visited Yangpinghua in Peng Prefecture and Sanxue Mountain in Han Prefecture.
value.literal: That year he also visited Yangpinghua in Peng Prefecture and Sanxue Mountain in Han Prefecture.

value.zh: 以王承休妻嚴氏故，十月，幸秦州，群臣切諫，衍不聽。
value.en: For the sake of Wang Chengxiu's wife Lady Yan, in the tenth month he visited Qin Prefecture. His ministers urgently remonstrated, but Yan would not listen.
value.literal: Because of Wang Chengxiu's wife Lady Yan, in the tenth month he visited Qin Prefecture; the ministers urgently remonstrated but Yan would not listen.

value.zh: 行至梓潼，大風發屋拔木，太史曰：「此貪狼風也，當有敗軍殺將者。」
value.en: At Zitong a great wind tore off roofs and uprooted trees. The grand astrologer said, "This is the Greedy Wolf wind—armies will be defeated and generals slain."
value.literal: Reaching Zitong, a great wind tore off roofs and uprooted trees. The grand astrologer said: "This is the Greedy Wolf wind—there will be defeated armies and slain generals."

value.zh: 衍不省。
value.en: Yan took no notice.
value.literal: Yan did not perceive it.

value.zh: 衍至綿谷而唐師入其境，衍懼，遽還。
value.en: When Yan reached Miangu and Tang troops entered Shu, he was alarmed and hurried back.
value.literal: When Yan reached Miangu and Tang troops entered his territory, Yan was afraid and hurried back.

value.zh: 唐師所至，州縣皆迎降。
value.en: Wherever Tang troops went, prefectures and counties welcomed them and submitted.
value.literal: Wherever Tang troops arrived, prefectures and counties all welcomed and submitted.

value.zh: 衍留王宗弼守綿谷，遣王宗勛、宗儼、宗昱率兵以拒唐師。
value.en: Yan left Wang Zongbi to hold Miangu and sent Wang Zongxun, Zongyan, and Zongyu with troops to resist Tang.
value.literal: Yan left Wang Zongbi to hold Miangu and sent Wang Zongxun, Zongyan, and Zongyu to lead troops against the Tang army.

value.zh: 宗勛等至三泉，望風退走。
value.en: Zongxun and the others reached Sanquan and fled at the first sight of Tang forces.
value.literal: Zongxun and the others reached Sanquan and fled at sight of the enemy.

value.zh: 衍詔宗弼誅宗勛等，宗弼反與宗勛等合謀，送款於唐師。
value.en: Yan ordered Zongbi to execute Zongxun and the others, but Zongbi instead conspired with them and submitted to Tang.
value.literal: Yan ordered Zongbi to execute Zongxun and the others; Zongbi instead joined in conspiracy with them and sent submission to the Tang army.

value.zh: 衍自綿谷還成都，百官及後宮迎謁七里亭，衍雜宮人作回鶻隊以入。
value.en: Yan returned from Miangu to Chengdu. Officials and palace women welcomed him at Qili Pavilion, and he entered the city mixed with palace women arrayed as a Uighur company.
value.literal: Yan returned from Miangu to Chengdu; the hundred officials and palace women welcomed him at Qili Pavilion, and Yan entered mixed with palace women formed as a Uighur company.

value.zh: 明日，禦文明殿，與其群臣相對涕泣。
value.en: The next day he held court at the Wenhua Hall and wept with his ministers face to face.
value.literal: The next day he held court at the Wenhua Hall and wept face to face with his ministers.

value.zh: 而宗弼亦自綿谷馳歸，登太玄門，收成都尹韓昭、宦者宋光嗣、景潤澄、歐陽晃等殺之，函首送於繼岌。
value.en: Zongbi also galloped back from Miangu, mounted the Taixuan Gate, seized and killed Chengdu prefect Han Zhao and the eunuchs Song Guangsi, Jing Runcheng, and Ouyang Huang, boxed their heads, and sent them to Jiji.
value.literal: Zongbi also galloped back from Miangu, mounted the Taixuan Gate, seized and killed Prefect of Chengdu Han Zhao and the eunuchs Song Guangsi, Jing Runcheng, and Ouyang Huang, boxed their heads and sent them to Jiji.

value.zh: 衍即上表乞降，宗弼遷衍於天啟宮。
value.en: Yan at once submitted a memorial begging to surrender, and Zongbi moved him to the Tianqi Palace.
value.literal: Yan forthwith submitted a memorial begging to surrender; Zongbi moved Yan to the Tianqi Palace.

value.zh: 魏王繼岌至成都，衍君臣面縛輿櫬，出降於七里亭。
value.en: When the Prince of Wei Jiji reached Chengdu, Yan and his court came out bound, carrying coffins, and surrendered at Qili Pavilion.
value.literal: When the Prince of Wei Jiji reached Chengdu, Yan and his court with faces bound and carrying coffins came out to surrender at Qili Pavilion.

value.zh: 莊宗召衍入洛，賜衍詔曰：「固當列土而封，必不薄人於險，三辰在上，一言不欺！」
value.en: Zhuangzong summoned Yan to Luoyang and bestowed an edict: "Surely you shall be enfeoffed with territory; surely no man shall be wronged in peril—the three luminaries are above, and not one word shall deceive!"
value.literal: Zhuangzong summoned Yan to Luoyang and bestowed an edict on him: "Surely territory shall be enfeoffed to you; surely no man shall be wronged in peril—the three luminaries are above, and not one word shall deceive!"

value.zh: 衍捧詔忻然就道，率其宗族及偽宰相王鍇、張格、瘐傳素、許寂、翰林學士李旻等，及諸將佐家族數千人以東。
value.en: Yan received the edict gladly and set out east with his clan, the former chief ministers Wang Kai, Zhang Ge, Yu Chuansu, Xu Ji, Hanlin academician Li Min, and the families of his generals and aides—several thousand people in all.
value.literal: Yan received the edict gladly and set out on the road, leading his clan and the false chief ministers Wang Kai, Zhang Ge, Yu Chuansu, Xu Ji, Hanlin Academician Li Min, and others, together with the families of generals and aides numbering several thousand, eastward.

value.zh: 同光四年四月，行至秦川驛，莊宗用伶人景進計，遣宦者向延嗣誅其族。
value.en: In the fourth month of Tongguang year 4, at Qinchuan Post Station, Zhuangzong followed the actor Jing Jin's advice and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to execute his entire clan.
value.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Tongguang, reaching Qinchuan Post Station, Zhuangzong used the actor Jing Jin's plan and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to execute his clan.

value.zh: 衍母徐氏臨刑呼曰：「吾兒以一國迎降，反以為戮，信義俱棄，吾知其禍不旋踵矣！」
value.en: Yan's mother Lady Xu cried out at the execution, "My son surrendered a whole state and is repaid with slaughter—faith and righteousness both cast aside. I know disaster will follow without delay!"
value.literal: Yan's mother Lady Xu cried out at execution: "My son surrendered a whole state and is repaid with slaughter—faith and righteousness both cast aside; I know disaster will not wait!"

value.zh: 衍妾劉氏，鬒發如雲而有色，行刑者將免之，劉氏曰：「家國喪亡，義不受辱！」
value.en: Yan's concubine Lady Liu, with hair black as clouds and great beauty, was about to be spared. She said, "State and house are lost—I will not accept disgrace!"
value.literal: Yan's concubine Lady Liu, with black hair like clouds and great beauty, was about to be spared by the executioners; Lady Liu said: "State and house are lost—by right I will not accept disgrace!"

value.zh: 遂就死。
value.en: She then went to her death.
value.literal: She then accepted death.

value.zh: 宗弼，本姓魏，名弘夫，建錄為養子。
value.en: Zongbi, born Wei Hongfu, was adopted by Jian.
value.literal: Zongbi, original surname Wei, name Hongfu, was recorded by Jian as an adopted son.

value.zh: 建攻顧彥暉，宗弼常以建語泄之彥暉者，彥暉敗，建待之如初。
value.en: When Jian attacked Gu Yanhui, Zongbi had often leaked Jian's plans to Yanhui. After Yanhui's defeat, Jian treated him as before.
value.literal: When Jian attacked Gu Yanhui, Zongbi had often leaked Jian's words to Yanhui; when Yanhui was defeated Jian treated him as before.

value.zh: 建病且卒，宗弼守太師兼中書令、判六軍，輔政。
value.en: When Jian fell ill near death, Zongbi served as grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat with charge of the Six Armies and assisted in government.
value.literal: When Jian was ill and near death, Zongbi held Grand Preceptor with concurrent Director of the Secretariat and charge of the Six Armies, assisting in government.

value.zh: 衍已降，宗弼以蜀珍寶奉魏王及郭崇韜，求為西川節度使，魏王曰：「此我家物也，何用獻為？」
value.en: After Yan surrendered, Zongbi presented Shu's treasures to the Prince of Wei and Guo Chongtao and asked to be made Xichuan military commissioner. The prince said, "These are my family's things—why present them?"
value.literal: After Yan had surrendered, Zongbi presented Shu's treasures to the Prince of Wei and Guo Chongtao and sought to be Xichuan military commissioner. The Prince of Wei said: "These are my family's things—why present them?"

value.zh: 居數日，為崇韜所殺。
value.en: A few days later Chongtao had him killed.
value.literal: After several days he was killed by Chongtao.

value.zh: 宗壽，許州民家子也。
value.en: Zongshou was the son of a common family in Xuzhou.
value.literal: Zongshou was the son of a common family in Xuzhou.

value.zh: 建以同姓，錄之為子。
value.en: Jian, sharing the surname Wang, adopted him as a son.
value.literal: Jian, because they shared a surname, recorded him as a son.

value.zh: 宗壽好學，工琴奕，為人恬退，喜道家之術，事建時為鎮江軍節度使。
value.en: Zongshou loved learning and was skilled at the zither and go. Retiring by nature, he favored Daoist practices and served Jian as military commissioner of the Zhenjiang army.
value.literal: Zongshou loved learning, was skilled at zither and go, by nature retiring and mild, fond of Daoist arts; while serving Jian he was military commissioner of the Zhenjiang Army.

value.zh: 衍既立，宗壽為太子太保奉朝請，以煉丹養氣自娛。
value.en: After Yan succeeded, Zongshou became junior guardian of the heir with court attendance and amused himself refining elixirs and cultivating breath.
value.literal: After Yan succeeded, Zongshou became Junior Guardian of the Heir with attendance at court, amusing himself with elixir refinement and nourishing breath.

value.zh: 衍為淫亂，獨宗壽常切諫之，後為武信軍節度使。
value.en: Yan was dissolute, and only Zongshou often remonstrated sharply. He later became military commissioner of the Wuxin army.
value.literal: Yan was dissolute; only Zongshou often remonstrated sharply, and later became military commissioner of the Wuxin Army.

value.zh: 唐師伐蜀，所在迎降，魏王嘗以書招之，獨宗壽不降。
value.en: When Tang invaded Shu, districts everywhere welcomed and submitted. The Prince of Wei once wrote to recruit him, but Zongshou alone refused.
value.literal: When Tang troops attacked Shu, wherever they went they were welcomed in submission; the Prince of Wei once sent a letter to recruit him, but Zongshou alone did not submit.

value.zh: 聞衍已銜璧，大慟，從衍東遷，至岐陽，以賂賂守者，得入見衍，衍泣下沾襟，曰：「早從王言，豈有今日！」
value.en: Hearing that Yan had already surrendered with the jade disk, he grieved greatly and followed him east. At Qiyang he bribed the guards and gained an audience. Yan wept until his robe was soaked and said, "Had I followed your counsel earlier, how could this day have come!"
value.literal: Hearing that Yan had already offered the jade disk in surrender, he grieved greatly and followed Yan eastward; reaching Qiyang, he bribed the guards and gained entry to see Yan. Yan wept until his breast was wet and said: "Had I early followed the prince's words, how could there be today!"

value.zh: 衍死，宗壽走澠池，聞莊宗遇弒，亡入熊耳山。
value.en: After Yan's death Zongshou fled to Mianchi. Hearing that Zhuangzong had been assassinated, he hid in Mount Xiong'er.
value.literal: After Yan's death Zongshou fled to Mianchi; hearing that Zhuangzong had been assassinated, he went into hiding in Mount Xiong'er.

value.zh: 天成二年，出詣京師，上書求衍宗族葬之。
value.en: In Tiancheng year 2 he emerged and went to the capital, submitting a memorial asking permission to bury Yan's clan.
value.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he came out and went to the capital, submitting a memorial asking to bury Yan's clan.

value.zh: 明宗嘉其忠，以為保義軍行軍司馬，封衍順正公，許以諸侯禮葬之。
value.en: Emperor Ming praised his loyalty, appointed him acting military secretary of the Baoyi army, enfeoffed him as Duke Shunzheng of Yan, and permitted burial with feudal honors.
value.literal: Emperor Ming praised his loyalty, made him acting military secretary of the Baoyi Army, enfeoffed Yan as Duke Shunzheng, and permitted burial with the rites of a feudal lord.

value.zh: 宗壽得王氏十八喪，葬之長安南三趙村。
value.en: Zongshou recovered the eighteen coffins of the Wang house and buried them at Sanzhao Village south of Chang'an.
value.literal: Zongshou obtained the eighteen coffins of the Wang house and buried them at Sanzhao Village south of Chang'an.

value.zh: 趙貴 獨孤信 侯莫陳崇
value.en: Zhao Gui — Du Guxin — Houmo Chen Chong
value.literal: Zhao Gui; Du Guxin; Houmo Chen Chong

value.zh: 大統三年秋，至長安。
value.en: In the autumn of Datong 3 (537) he reached Chang'an.
value.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Datong, he reached Chang'an.

value.zh: 自以虧損國威，上書謝罪。
value.en: Believing he had shamed the state, he wrote to apologize for his failure.
value.literal: Considering himself to have diminished the state's prestige, he submitted a memorial apologizing for his offense.

value.zh: 魏文帝付尚書議之，七兵尚書、陳郡王
value.en: Emperor Wen of Wei referred the matter to the Masters of Writing—the Minister of the Seven Armies, Prince of Chen commandery
value.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei handed the matter to the Masters of Writing for deliberation—the Minister of the Seven Armies, Prince of Chen commandery

value.zh: （王言）
value.en: [variant: Wang Yan]
value.literal: (Wang Yan)

value.zh: 玄等議，以為「邊將董戎，龔行天罰，喪師敗績，國刑無舍。
value.en: Xuan and others deliberated, saying: "Frontier generals who bear Heaven's mandate to chastise wrongdoers and yet lose their armies—the law knows no mercy.
value.literal: Xuan and others deliberated, saying: "Frontier generals who marshal troops and carry Heaven's punishment—when they lose the army and fail in the campaign, the state punishment allows no pardon.

value.zh: 荊州刺史獨孤如願，任當推轂，遠襲襄、宛，斬賊帥辛纂，傳首京師，論功語效，寔合嘉賞。
value.en: Jing Province governor Du Guxin, entrusted with full command, had raided deep into Xiang and Wan, beheaded the rebel leader Xin Zuan, and sent his head to the capital—a feat that plainly merited reward.
value.literal: Jing Province governor Dugu Ruyuan, his charge being to push the chariot, made a distant raid on Xiang and Wan, beheaded the bandit chief Xin Zuan, and sent his head to the capital; in reckoning merit and speaking of achievement, he truly deserved fine reward.

value.zh: 但庸績不終，旋致淪沒，責成之義，朝寄有違。
value.en: Yet his success was not sustained and he was soon lost; by the rule that a commission must be fulfilled, he had failed the court's trust.
value.literal: Yet meritorious deeds were not carried through and he soon fell into ruin; the principle of completing the charge—the court's trust was violated.

value.zh: 然孤軍數千，後援未接，賊衆我寡，難以自固。
value.en: Still, he had only a few thousand men with no reinforcements, outnumbered and unable to stand alone.
value.literal: Still, a lone army of several thousand with rear support not yet joined—bandits many, we few—it was hard to hold firm on one's own.

value.zh: 旣經恩降，理絕刑書。
value.en: Grace had already been shown him, so the penal code no longer applied.
value.literal: Since grace in reduction of punishment had already been granted, reason excludes the criminal code.

value.zh: 昔秦宥孟明，漢舍廣利，卒能改過立功，垂芳竹帛。
value.en: Qin once spared Meng Ming and Han forgave Li Guangli; both went on to redeem themselves and win lasting fame.
value.literal: Formerly Qin pardoned Meng Ming and Han spared Guangli; in the end they were able to reform their faults and establish merit, leaving fragrance in the bamboo and silk.

value.zh: 以今方古，抑有成規。
value.en: Comparing present with past, there was clear precedent.
value.literal: Measuring the present against antiquity, there is indeed an established rule.

value.zh: 臣等參議，請赦罪，復其舊職」。
value.en: We your ministers therefore ask that his offense be pardoned and his former office restored."
value.literal: We your ministers jointly deliberate: we request pardon of the offense and restoration to his former office."

value.zh: 魏文帝詔曰：「如願荊、襄之役，寔展功效。
value.en: Emperor Wen of Wei decreed: "Du Guxin's campaign in Jing and Xiang did show real service.
value.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei decreed: "Ruyuan's Jing and Xiang campaign truly displayed achievement.

value.zh: 旣屬強寇，力屈道窮，歸賊不可，還朝路絕，適事求宜，未足稱過。
value.en: He met a powerful enemy, was spent, and could neither submit to the foe nor find a way home—given the circumstances, he can hardly be blamed.
value.literal: Having encountered a strong foe, his strength bent and the way was exhausted; to return to the bandits was impossible and the road back to court was cut off—seeking what suited the affair, it is insufficient to call it fault.

value.zh: 違難如吳，誠貫夷險，義全終始，良可嘉歎。
value.en: He bore hardship through every danger with constancy from first to last—truly admirable.
value.literal: Enduring hardship like Wu, his sincerity penetrating easy and perilous, his righteousness complete from beginning to end—truly worthy of praise and sighing admiration.

value.zh: 復情存謙退，款心謝責。
value.en: He had shown humility and offered a sincere apology.
value.literal: Again, his feeling preserved humility and withdrawal; with sincere heart he declined blame.

value.zh: 甯容議及恩降，止雲免咎，斯則事失權宜，理乖通變。
value.en: To treat this as no more than a pardon from punishment falls short of what the moment requires.
value.literal: How could one allow the deliberation to reach only to grace in reduction of punishment and stop at saying merely exemption from blame? That then is the affair losing what suits the moment and reason departing from flexible change.

value.zh: 可轉驃騎大將軍，加侍中、開府，其使持節、儀同三司、浮陽郡公悉如故。」
value.en: Let him be made grand general of agile cavalry, with attendant-in-ordinary and opening-the-feudatory added; his staff, three-division court equipage, and ducal title of Fuyang shall all stand as before."
value.literal: He may be transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with the added posts of attendant-in-ordinary and opening-the-feudatory; his bearer of the staff, three-division court equipage, and Duke of Fuyang commandery shall all remain as before."

value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 131
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 131

value.zh: 丁卯，吳喜至錢唐，孔璪、王曇生奔浙東。
value.en: On dingmao, Wu Xi reached Qiantang; Kong Zuan and Wang Tansheng fled into eastern Zhe.
value.literal: On dingmao, Wu Xi reached Qiantang; Kong Zuan and Wang Tansheng fled to eastern Zhe.

value.zh: 喜遣強弩將軍任農夫等引兵向黃山浦；
value.en: Xi sent Strong Crossbow general Ren Nongfu and others toward Huangshan Ford;
value.literal: Xi sent Strong Crossbow General Ren Nongfu and others to lead troops toward Huangshan Ford;

value.zh: 東軍據岸結寨，農夫等擊破之。
value.en: the eastern army held the bank and built stockades; Nongfu and his men attacked and broke them.
value.literal: the eastern army held the bank and built stockades; Nongfu and the others attacked and broke them.

value.zh: 喜自柳浦渡，取西陵，擊斬庚業。
value.en: Xi crossed from Liupu, took Xiling, and attacked and beheaded Geng Ye.
value.literal: Xi crossed from Liupu, took Xiling, and attacked and beheaded Geng Ye.

value.zh: 會稽人大懼，將士多奔亡，孔凱不能制。
value.en: The people of Kuaiji were terrified; officers and soldiers fled in droves; Kong Kai could not control them.
value.literal: The people of Kuaiji were greatly afraid; officers and soldiers mostly fled; Kong Kai could not control them.

value.zh: 戊寅，上虞令王晏起兵攻郡，凱逃奔脊山；
value.en: On wuyin, Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops against the commandery; Kong Kai fled to Jishan;
value.literal: On wuyin, Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops to attack the commandery; Kai fled to Jishan;

value.zh: 車騎從事中郎張綏封府庫以待吳喜。
value.en: Chief clerk to the general of chariots and cavalry Zhang Sui sealed the government treasury to await Wu Xi.
value.literal: Chief Clerk to the General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Sui sealed the government treasury to await Wu Xi.

value.zh: 己卯，王晏入城，殺綏，執尋陽王子房於別署。
value.en: On jimao, Wang Yan entered the city, killed Zhang Sui, and seized Prince of Xunyang Liu Zifang at a separate residence.
value.literal: On jimao, Wang Yan entered the city, killed Sui, and seized Prince of Xunyang Zifang at a separate residence.

value.zh: 縱兵大掠，府庫皆空；
value.en: He let his troops plunder freely; the treasury was emptied;
value.literal: He let the troops plunder freely; the treasury was emptied;

value.zh: 獲孔璪，殺之。
value.en: they captured Kong Zuan and killed him.
value.literal: they captured Kong Zuan and killed him.

value.zh: 庚辰，脊山民縛孔凱送晏，晏謂之曰：「此事孔璪所為，無預卿事，可作首辭，當相為申上。」
value.en: On gengchen, the people of Jishan bound Kong Kai and sent him to Wang Yan; Yan said to him: "This was Kong Zuan's doing and does not involve you; draft a confession and I will present it for you at court."
value.literal: On gengchen, the people of Jishan bound Kong Kai and sent him to Yan; Yan said to him: "This affair was Kong Zuan's doing; it does not involve you; you may compose a memorial of confession and I shall present it on your behalf to the throne."

value.zh: 凱曰：「江東處分，莫不由身；
value.en: Kong Kai said: "Every decision in the Jiangdong region was mine alone;
value.literal: Kai said: "Every disposition in Jiangdong was none other than my own;

value.zh: 委罪求活，便是君輩行意耳。」
value.en: to shift blame to save my skin—that is exactly your sort's way."
value.literal: to shift blame to seek life—that is precisely your sort's intent."

value.zh: 晏乃斬之。
value.en: Yan then beheaded him.
value.literal: Yan then beheaded him.

value.zh: 顧琛、王曇生、袁標等詣吳喜歸罪，喜皆宥之。
value.en: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others came to Wu Xi to surrender; Xi pardoned them all.
value.literal: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others came to Wu Xi to surrender blame; Xi pardoned them all.

value.zh: 東軍主凡七十六人，於陳斬十七人，其餘皆原宥。
value.en: Of seventy-six eastern army commanders in all, seventeen were beheaded in battle; the rest were all pardoned.
value.literal: Eastern army commanders numbered seventy-six in all; seventeen were beheaded in the array; the rest were all pardoned.

value.en: jiazi, corresponding to 484 CE)
value.literal: jiazi, the year 484 CE)

value.zh: 范縝盛稱無佛。
value.en: Fan Zhen loudly maintained that there is no Buddha.
value.literal: Fan Zhen loudly proclaimed that there is no Buddha.

value.zh: 子良曰：「君不信因果，何得有富貴、貧賤？」
value.en: Ziliang said, "If you do not believe in karma, how can there be rich and poor?"
value.literal: Ziliang said, "If you do not believe in cause and effect, how can there be wealth and honor, poverty and low estate?"

value.zh: 縝曰：「人生如樹花同發，隨風而散：或拂簾幌墜茵席之上，或關籬牆落糞溷之中。
value.en: Zhen replied, "Human life is like flowers on a tree blooming at once and scattering in the wind—some brush the curtain and land on cushions, others hit the fence and fall into the dung pit.
value.literal: Zhen said, "Human life is like blossoms on a tree blooming together and scattering with the wind: some brush the curtain and fall on cushions and mats, some strike the fence and fall into the privy.

value.zh: 墜茵席者，殿下是也；
value.en: Those who land on cushions—that is you, my lord;
value.literal: Those who fall on cushions and mats—that is Your Highness;

value.zh: 落糞溷者，下官是也。
value.en: those who fall into the dung pit—that is this humble official.
value.literal: those who fall into the privy—that is this humble official.

value.zh: 貴賤雖復殊途，因果竟在何處！」
value.en: Noble and base may take different paths—where then is karma!"
value.literal: Noble and base may take different paths, but where after all is cause and effect!"

value.zh: 子良無以難。
value.en: Ziliang had no answer.
value.literal: Ziliang had nothing with which to refute him.

value.zh: 縝又著《神滅論》，以為：「形者神之質，神者形之用也。
value.en: Zhen also wrote "On the Destruction of the Soul," arguing that "the body is the substance of the spirit, and the spirit is the function of the body.
value.literal: Zhen also wrote "On the Destruction of the Soul," holding that "the body is the substance of the spirit; the spirit is the function of the body.

value.zh: 神之於形，猶利之於刀；
value.en: The spirit in relation to the body is like sharpness to a blade;
value.literal: The spirit in relation to the body is like sharpness in relation to a knife;

value.zh: 未聞刀沒而利存，豈容形亡而神在哉！」
value.en: no one has heard of the blade vanishing while sharpness remains—how then could the body perish while the spirit endures!"
value.literal: one has never heard of the knife perishing while sharpness remains—how could the body perish while the spirit endures!"

value.zh: 此論出，朝野喧嘩，難之，終不能屈。
value.en: When the treatise appeared, court and country were in an uproar; critics assailed it, but none could refute him in the end.
value.literal: When this treatise appeared, court and countryside clamored; many challenged it, but in the end none could overcome him.

value.zh: 太原王琰著論譏縝曰：「嗚呼范子！
value.en: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise mocking Zhen: "Alas, Master Fan!
value.literal: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise to mock Zhen, saying, "Alas, Master Fan!

value.zh: 曾不知其先祖神靈所在！」
value.en: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"
value.literal: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"

value.zh: 欲以杜縝後對。
value.en: He meant to silence any reply from Zhen.
value.literal: He wished thereby to block Zhen from replying.

value.zh: 縝對曰：「嗚呼王子！
value.en: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!
value.literal: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!

value.zh: 知其先祖神靈所在，而不能殺身以從之！」
value.en: You know where your ancestors' spirits abide, yet you cannot kill yourself to join them!"
value.literal: You know where the spirits of your ancestors abide, yet cannot kill yourself to follow them!"

value.zh: 子良使王融謂之曰：「以卿才美，何患不至中書郎；
value.en: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent, why should you fail to reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;
value.literal: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent and beauty, why worry that you will not reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;

value.zh: 而故乖剌為此論，甚可惜也！
value.en: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how regrettable!
value.literal: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how very regrettable!

value.zh: 宜急毀棄之。」
value.en: You should destroy it at once."
value.literal: You should hurry to destroy and abandon it."

value.zh: 縝大笑曰：「使范縝賣論取官，已至令、僕矣，何但中書郎邪！」
value.en: Zhen laughed and said, "If Fan Zhen sold his thesis for office, he would already be Minister or Vice Minister—why settle for mere Director of the Palace Secretariat!"
value.literal: Zhen laughed loudly and said, "If Fan Zhen were to sell his thesis for office, he would already have reached Minister and Vice Minister—why only Director of the Palace Secretariat!"

value.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明七年（
value.en: Emperor Wu of Qi (first section, lower part), Yongming year 7 (
value.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 7 (

value.zh: 初，上為鎮西長史，主簿王晏以傾諂為上所親，自是常在上府。
value.en: Earlier, when the emperor was Chief Clerk of the Army of the West, Registrar Wang Yan won his favor through sycophantic flattery and thereafter remained constantly at his headquarters.
value.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was Chief Clerk of the Army of the West, Registrar Wang Yan won the emperor's favor through fawning flattery; from then on he was constantly at the prince's headquarters.

value.zh: 上為太子，晏為中庶子。
value.en: When the emperor became heir apparent, Yan was made Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: When the emperor became heir apparent, Yan became Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 上之得罪於太祖也，晏稱疾自疏。
value.en: When the emperor fell from favor with the Founding Emperor, Yan feigned illness and distanced himself.
value.literal: When the emperor fell from favor with the Founding Emperor, Yan pleaded illness and kept his distance.

value.zh: 及即位，為丹陽尹，意任如舊，朝夕進見，議論朝事；
value.en: After the emperor took the throne, Yan was made Governor of Danyang; the emperor trusted him as before and received him morning and evening to discuss affairs of state;
value.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Yan was made Governor of Danyang; the emperor's trust in him was as before, and he was received morning and evening to discuss court affairs;

value.zh: 自豫章王嶷及王儉皆降意接之。
value.en: From Prince Liao of Yuzhang down to Wang Jian, all showed deference in receiving him.
value.literal: From Prince Liao of Yuzhang down to Wang Jian, all lowered themselves to receive him graciously.

value.zh: 二月，壬寅，出為江州刺史；
value.en: In the second month, on renyin, he was appointed Inspector of Jiang Province;
value.literal: In the second month, on renyin, he was sent out as Inspector of Jiang Province;

value.zh: 晏不願外出，復留為吏部尚書。
value.en: Yan did not wish to leave the capital and was kept on as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
value.literal: Yan did not wish to go out on assignment and was again retained as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

value.zh: 三月，甲寅，立皇子子岳為臨賀王，子峻為廣漢王，子琳為宣城王，子鈱為義安王。
value.en: In the third month, on jiayin, the emperor enfeoffed his sons Ziyue as Prince of Linhe, Zijun as Prince of Guanghan, Zilin as Prince of Xuancheng, and Zimin as Prince of Yi'an.
value.literal: In the third month, on jiayin, the emperor enfeoffed his sons Ziyue as Prince of Linhe, Zijun as Prince of Guanghan, Zilin as Prince of Xuancheng, and Zimin as Prince of Yi'an.

value.zh: 五月，乙巳，儉卒。
value.en: In the fifth month, on yisi, Wang Jian died.
value.literal: In the fifth month, on yisi, Jian died.

value.zh: 王晏既領選，權行台閣，與儉頗不平。
value.en: Wang Yan, now in charge of personnel selection, exercised the powers of the Secretariat and was on bad terms with Jian.
value.literal: Wang Yan, having taken charge of selection, wielded the authority of the Secretariat and was on rather poor terms with Jian.

value.zh: 禮官欲依王導，謚儉為文獻。
value.en: The ritual officials wished to follow the precedent of Wang Dao and posthumously name Jian Literary Paragon.
value.literal: The ritual officials wished to follow the precedent of Wang Dao and give Jian the posthumous title Literary Paragon.

value.zh: 晏啟上曰：「導乃得此謚；
value.en: Yan memorialized the emperor, saying, "Only Wang Dao deserved that posthumous title;
value.literal: Yan memorialized the emperor, saying, "Only Dao deserved this posthumous title;

value.zh: 但宋氏以來，不加異姓。」
value.en: since the Song, such titles have not been granted to men of a different surname;"
value.literal: since the Song dynasty, such titles have not been granted to those of a different surname;"

value.zh: 出，謂親人曰：「『平頭憲』事已行矣。」
value.en: After leaving, he told his intimates, "The affair of the 'Flat-Xian' title is already settled."
value.literal: After leaving, he told his intimates, "The affair of the 'truncated Xian' has already been settled."

value.zh: 上欲用領軍王奐為尚書令，以問王晏。
value.en: The emperor wished to appoint Commandant of the Guards Wang Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and consulted Wang Yan.
value.literal: The emperor wished to appoint Commandant of the Guards Wang Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and asked Wang Yan about it.

value.zh: 晏與奐不相能，對曰：「柳世隆有勳望，恐不宜在奐後。」
value.en: Yan was on bad terms with Huan and replied, "Liu Shilong has both merit and prestige; it would hardly be fitting to rank him below Huan."
value.literal: Yan was on bad terms with Huan and replied, "Liu Shilong has merit and prestige; I fear it would not be fitting to place him after Huan."

value.zh: 甲子，以尚書左僕射柳世隆為尚書令，王奐為左僕射。
value.en: On jiazi, Left Vice Director Liu Shilong was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Wang Huan was made Left Vice Director.
value.literal: On jiazi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Shilong was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Wang Huan was made Left Vice Director.
