value.zh: 西昌侯鸞既誅徐龍駒、周奉叔，而尼媼外入者，頗傳異語。
value.en: After Luan, Marquis of Xichang, had killed Xu Longju and Zhou Fengshu, nuns and old women coming in from outside spread all manner of alarming rumors.
value.literal: After Luan, Marquis of Xichang, had executed Xu Longju and Zhou Fengshu, nuns and old women entering from outside rather widely spread strange talk.

value.zh: 中書令何胤，以後之從叔，為帝所親，使直殿省。
value.en: He Yin, Director of the Secretariat, was a maternal uncle of the empress and a favorite of the emperor, who had him serve in the Hall Directorate.
value.literal: Director of the Secretariat He Yin, being a paternal uncle on the empress's side, was intimate with the emperor and was made to attend the Hall Directorate.

value.zh: 帝與胤謀誅鸞，令胤受事；
value.en: The emperor plotted with Yin to kill Luan and told Yin to take charge;
value.literal: The emperor with Yin plotted to kill Luan and ordered Yin to take charge of the matter;

value.zh: 胤不敢當，依違諫說，帝意復止。
value.en: Yin did not dare accept the role; he hedged and urged caution, and the emperor's resolve faded again.
value.literal: Yin did not dare undertake it, vacillating with admonitory persuasion, and the emperor's intent again ceased.

value.zh: 乃謀出鸞於西州，中敕用事，不復關咨於鸞。
value.en: They then planned to post Luan away to Western Province so that central orders would govern affairs without consulting him.
value.literal: Then they plotted to send Luan out to Western Province; central edicts would govern affairs, no longer consulting Luan.

value.zh: 是時，蕭諶、蕭坦之握兵權，左僕射王晏總尚書事。
value.en: At this time Chen and Tanzhi controlled the army, while Wang Yan, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, oversaw the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: At this time Chen and Tanzhi held military authority; Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat Wang Yan oversaw Masters of Writing affairs.

value.zh: 諶密召諸王典簽，約語之，不許諸王外接人物。
value.en: Chen secretly summoned each prince's chief clerk, bound them by agreement, and forbade the princes to receive outsiders.
value.literal: Chen secretly summoned the palace stewards of the princes, made agreements with them, not permitting the princes to receive people from outside.

value.zh: 諶親要日久，眾皆憚而從之。
value.en: Chen had long been close to power, and everyone feared him and complied.
value.literal: Chen had been intimate and influential for many days; all feared him and obeyed.

value.zh: 鸞以其謀告王晏，晏聞之，響應；
value.en: Luan disclosed his plan to Wang Yan, who at once assented;
value.literal: Luan reported his plot to Wang Yan; Yan on hearing it responded in agreement;

value.zh: 又告丹陽尹徐孝嗣，孝嗣亦從之。
value.en: He also informed Xu Xiaosi, governor of Danyang, and Xiaosi went along as well.
value.literal: He also told Xu Xiaosi, governor of Danyang; Xiaosi also followed.

value.zh: 驃騎錄事南陽樂豫謂孝嗣曰：「外傳籍籍，似有伊、周之事。
value.en: Leyu of Nanyang, recorder on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General, told Xiaosi: "Rumors are everywhere, as though someone were playing Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou to the throne.
value.literal: Recorder of Affairs under the Rapid Cavalry General Leyu of Nanyang said to Xiaosi: "Outside the talk is widespread, as if there were an Yi Yin and Duke of Zhou affair.

value.zh: 君蒙武帝殊常之恩，荷托附之重，恐不得同人此舉。
value.en: You received extraordinary favor from Emperor Wu and bore a heavy trust; I fear you cannot join them in this.
value.literal: You received Emperor Wu's exceptional grace, bore the weight of entrustment— I fear you cannot go along with this action in common with them.

value.zh: 人笑褚公，至今齒冷。」
value.en: Men still mock Lord Chu, and the mockery has not grown stale."
value.literal: People still laugh at Lord Chu; to this day teeth are cold."

value.zh: 孝嗣心然之，而不能從。
value.en: Xiaosi agreed in his heart but could not bring himself to refuse.
value.literal: Xiaosi inwardly agreed but could not refuse to follow.

value.zh: 帝謂蕭坦之曰：「人言鎮軍與王晏、蕭諶欲共廢我，似非虛傳。
value.en: The emperor said to Tanzhi: "People say the General Who Guards the Army, Wang Yan, and Chen are plotting to depose me together. That does not sound like idle talk.
value.literal: The emperor said to Tanzhi: "People say the General Who Guards the Army with Wang Yan and Xiao Chen together wish to depose me— it does not seem a false rumor.

value.zh: 卿所聞雲何？」
value.en: What have you heard on your side?"
value.literal: What have you heard?"

value.zh: 坦之曰：「天下寧當有此，誰樂無事廢天子邪！
value.en: Tanzhi replied: "Could such a thing truly happen in the world? Who would want to depose the Son of Heaven when nothing is amiss!
value.literal: Tanzhi said: "Would such a thing really exist under Heaven— who would delight in deposing the Son of Heaven when there is nothing wrong!

value.zh: 朝貴不容造此論，當是諸尼姥言耳，豈有信邪！
value.en: The great officials of court would never invent such talk; it must be those nuns and old women. How could anyone believe it!
value.literal: Court nobles would not allow such talk to be made; it must be the words of those nuns and old women— how could there be belief!

value.zh: 官若無事除此二人，誰敢自保！」
value.en: If Your Majesty removed these two men without cause, who would dare think himself safe!"
value.literal: If Your Majesty without cause removed these two men, who would dare protect himself!"

value.zh: 直閣將軍曹道剛疑外間有異，密有處分，謀未能發。
value.en: Cao Daogang, Director of the Palace Gate, suspected trouble outside and made secret arrangements, but the plot never came off.
value.literal: Director of the Palace Gate Cao Daogang suspected something unusual outside, had secret dispositions, but the plot could not be launched.

value.zh: 壬辰，鸞使蕭諶先入宮，遇曹道剛及中書舍人朱隆之，皆殺之。
value.en: On the renchen day, Luan sent Chen into the palace ahead of him; Chen met Cao Daogang and Zhu Longzhi, Master of Writing Attendant, and killed them both.
value.literal: On day renchen, Luan sent Chen to enter the palace first; encountering Cao Daogang and Master of Writing Attendant Zhu Longzhi, he killed them both.

value.zh: 直後徐僧亮盛怒，大言於眾曰：「吾等荷恩，今日應死報！」
value.en: Xu Sengliang, palace attendant, flew into a rage and cried out to those around him: "We owe the emperor our lives; today we must repay him with death!"
value.literal: Palace Attendant Xu Sengliang was greatly enraged and spoke loudly before the crowd: "We have received grace; today we should repay with death!"

value.zh: 又殺之。
value.en: He too was killed.
value.literal: He was killed as well.

value.zh: 鸞引兵自尚書入雲龍門，戎服加朱衣於上，比入門，三失履。
value.en: Luan led his troops from the Masters of Writing compound through the Cloud Dragon Gate, wearing armor with a vermilion robe over it; before he crossed the threshold he lost his shoes three times.
value.literal: Luan led troops from the Masters of Writing into the Cloud Dragon Gate, military dress with vermilion robe over it; by the time he entered the gate he had lost his shoes three times.

value.zh: 王晏、徐孝嗣、蕭坦之、陳顯達、王廣之、沈文季皆隨其後。
value.en: Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, and Shen Wenji all followed in his train.
value.literal: Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, and Shen Wenji all followed behind him.

value.zh: 帝在壽昌殿。
value.en: The emperor was in the Hall of Longevity and Prosperity.
value.literal: The emperor was in the Shouchang Hall.

value.zh: 聞外有變，猶密為手敕呼蕭諶，又使閉內殿諸房閣。
value.en: When he heard trouble outside, he still secretly drafted a personal order summoning Chen and had the inner chambers and side halls barred.
value.literal: Hearing there was disturbance outside, he still secretly made a hand edict summoning Chen, and also ordered the inner hall rooms and pavilions closed.

value.zh: 俄而諶引兵入壽昌閣，帝走趨徐姬房，拔劍自刺，不入，以帛纏頸，輿接出延德殿。
value.en: Soon Chen marched into the Shouchang Pavilion. The emperor fled to Lady Xu's rooms, tried to stab himself but failed, bound his neck in silk, and was carried out on a litter to the Hall of Extended Virtue.
value.literal: Before long Chen led troops into the Shouchang Pavilion; the emperor ran to Lady Xu's quarters, drew his sword to stab himself but did not penetrate, wrapped his neck in silk, and was carried out by litter to the Yande Hall.

value.zh: 諶初入殿，宿衛將士皆操弓楯欲拒戰。
value.en: When Chen first entered the hall, the palace guards seized bows and shields, ready to fight.
value.literal: When Chen first entered the hall, the palace guards all grasped bows and shields wishing to resist and fight.

value.zh: 諶謂之曰：「所取自有人，卿等不須動！」
value.en: Chen told them: "We are only taking the man we came for; none of you need stir!"
value.literal: Chen said to them: "The one taken has his own person; you need not move!"

value.zh: 宿衛素隸服於諶，皆信之，及見帝出，各欲自奮，帝竟無一言。
value.en: The guards had long served under Chen and trusted him. When they saw the emperor led away, several wanted to fight, but the emperor never spoke a word.
value.literal: The palace guards had long been subordinate to Chen and all believed him; when they saw the emperor brought out, each wished to exert himself, but the emperor in the end said not a word.

value.zh: 行至西弄，弒之。
value.en: At the western passage they murdered him.
value.literal: When they reached the western lane, they assassinated him.

value.zh: 輿屍出殯徐龍駒宅，葬以王禮。
value.en: They carried his body out and laid it in state at Xu Longju's house, then buried him with the honors due a prince.
value.literal: They carried the corpse out and encoffined it at Xu Longju's residence, burying him with princely rites.

value.zh: 徐姬及諸嬖倖皆伏誅。
value.en: Lady Xu and all the emperor's favorites were put to death.
value.literal: Lady Xu and all the favored minions were executed.

value.zh: 鸞既執帝，欲作太后令；
value.en: Once Luan held the emperor captive, he wanted to issue an order in the empress dowager's name;
value.literal: After Luan had seized the emperor, he wished to draft an empress dowager order;

value.zh: 徐孝嗣於袖中出而進之，鸞大悅。
value.en: Xu Xiaosi drew the draft from his sleeve and submitted it, and Luan was delighted.
value.literal: Xu Xiaosi produced it from his sleeve and presented it; Luan was greatly pleased.

value.zh: 癸巳，以太后令追廢帝為鬱林王，又廢何後為王妃，迎立新安王昭文。
value.en: On the guisi day, by order of the empress dowager the emperor was posthumously demoted to Prince of Yulin, Empress He was reduced to princess consort, and Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, was installed on the throne.
value.literal: On day guisi, by empress dowager order the emperor was posthumously deposed as Prince of Yulin, Empress He was also deposed as princess consort, and Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, was welcomed and established.

value.zh: 八月，甲辰，以司空王敬則為太尉。
value.en: In the eighth month, on the jiachen day, Wang Jingze, Minister of Works, was appointed Grand Commandant.
value.literal: Eighth month, jiachen, Wang Jingze, Minister of Works, was made Grand Commandant.

value.zh: 鄱陽王鏘為司徒，車騎大將軍陳顯達為司空，尚書左僕射王晏為尚書令。
value.en: Xiao Qiang, Prince of Poyang, became Minister of Education; Chen Xianda, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, became Minister of Works; and Wang Yan, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, became Director of the Secretariat.
value.literal: Xiao Qiang, Prince of Poyang, was made Minister of Education; Chen Xianda, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, was made Minister of Works; Wang Yan, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, was made Director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 魏主至陰山。
value.en: The Wei emperor reached Yin Mountain.
value.literal: The Wei emperor reached Yin Mountain.

value.zh: 海陵王在位，起居飲食，皆咨宣城王而後行。
value.en: While Prince Hailing sat on the throne, every act of daily life—rising, resting, eating, drinking—required the Prince of Xuancheng's approval.
value.literal: The Prince of Hailing, on the throne, in rising, resting, eating, and drinking—all consulted the Prince of Xuancheng before acting.

value.zh: 嘗思食蒸魚菜，太官令答無錄公命，竟不與。
value.en: Once he craved steamed fish and greens; the palace provisioner answered that without the Chief Recorder's command nothing could be served, and he went without.
value.literal: He once wished to eat steamed fish and vegetables; the Grand Provisioner replied that without the Chief Recorder's order, in the end it was not given.

value.zh: 辛亥，皇太后令曰：「嗣主沖幼，庶政多昧；
value.en: On xinhai the Empress Dowager issued an edict: "The heir to the throne is young, and public affairs are beyond him;
value.literal: On day xinhai, the Empress Dowager's order said: "The successor ruler is young and tender, and the many affairs of government are obscure;

value.zh: 且早嬰尪疾，弗克負荷。
value.en: moreover he has been frail from childhood and cannot bear the burden of rule.
value.literal: moreover, from early youth he has been afflicted with wasting illness and cannot bear the burden.

value.zh: 太傅宣城王，胤體宣皇，鐘慈太祖，宜入承寶命。
value.en: Grand Tutor the Prince of Xuancheng, born of the imperial line and cherished by the founding emperor, should ascend and receive the Mandate.
value.literal: Grand Tutor the Prince of Xuancheng, by blood-line the body of the Proclaimed Emperor, concentrating kindness from the Grand Ancestor, ought to enter and receive the precious mandate.

value.zh: 帝可降封海陵王，吾當歸老別館。」
value.en: Let the emperor be demoted to Prince Hailing; I shall retire to a separate palace."
value.literal: The emperor may be demoted and enfeoffed as Prince of Hailing; I shall return to age in a separate lodge."

value.zh: 且以宣城王為太祖第三子。
value.en: The court also declared the Prince of Xuancheng to be the founding emperor's third son.
value.literal: Moreover, the Prince of Xuancheng was treated as the Grand Ancestor's third son.

value.zh: 癸亥，高宗即皇帝位，大赦，改元。
value.en: On guihai Emperor Ming took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.
value.literal: On day guihai, the High Ancestor assumed the imperial position, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

value.zh: 以太尉王敬則為大司馬，司空陳顯達為太尉，尚書令王晏加驃騎大將軍，左僕射徐孝嗣加中軍大將軍，中領軍蕭諶為領軍將軍。
value.en: Wang Jingze was made Grand Marshal, Chen Xianda Grand Commandant, Wang Yan Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Xu Xiaosi General of the Central Army, and Xiao Zhen Commander of the Palace Guards.
value.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Jingze was made Grand Marshal; Minister of Works Chen Xianda was made Grand Commandant; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was added as Rapid Cavalry Grand General; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi was added as General of the Central Army; Central Palace Guard Commander Xiao Zhen was made Commander of the Palace Guards.

value.zh: 度支尚書虞悰稱疾不陪位。
value.en: Yu Song, Minister of Revenue, pleaded illness and did not attend the enthronement.
value.literal: Minister of Revenue Yu Song claimed illness and did not attend the enthronement.

value.zh: 帝以悰舊人，欲引參佐命，使王晏繼廢立事示悰。
value.en: The emperor, knowing Song as an old associate, wished to enlist him in the new order and had Wang Yan recount the deposition and enthronement for his benefit.
value.literal: The emperor, because Song was an old acquaintance, wished to draw him in to assist the mandate; he had Wang Yan continue the account of deposition and enthronement to show Song.

value.zh: 悰曰：「主上聖明，公卿戮力，寧假朽老以贊惟新乎！
value.en: Song said: "Your Majesty is sage and brilliant, and the ministers serve with one accord—why borrow a worn-out old man for the renewal of the state!
value.literal: Song said: "The ruler above is sagely and bright, the dukes and ministers exert their strength together—how could one borrow a decayed old man to assist the renewal!

value.zh: 不敢聞命！」
value.en: I dare not accept such a command!"
value.literal: dare not hear command!"

value.zh: 因慟哭。
value.en: And thereupon he broke into bitter weeping.
value.literal: thereupon wailed in grief.

value.zh: 朝議欲糾之，徐孝嗣曰：「此亦古之遺直。」
value.en: The court debated punishing him; Xu Xiaosi said, "This, too, is a remnant of the ancient type who spoke straight to power."
value.literal: court deliberation wished to impeach him, Xu Xiaosi said: "this also is antiquity's surviving straightness."

value.zh: 乃止。
value.en: And they desisted.
value.literal: then stopped.

value.zh: 帝與群臣宴會，詔功臣上酒。
value.en: The emperor feasted with his ministers and ordered meritorious officials to offer toasts.
value.literal: emperor with ministers banquet, ordered meritorious ministers offer wine.

value.zh: 王晏等興席，謝瀹獨不起，曰：「陛下受命，應天順人；
value.en: Wang Yan and the others rose from their seats; Xie Yue alone remained seated and said, "Your Majesty received the Mandate, harmonizing with Heaven and following the people;
value.literal: Wang Yan and others rose from seats, Xie Yue alone did not rise, said: "Your Majesty received Mandate, responded to Heaven followed people;

value.zh: 王晏妄叨天功以為己力！」
value.en: Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own achievement!"
value.literal: Wang Yan presumptuously usurps Heaven's merit as his own strength!"

value.zh: 帝大笑，解之。
value.en: The emperor laughed heartily and let the matter pass.
value.literal: emperor great laugh, excused him.

value.zh: 座罷，晏呼瀹共載還令省，欲相撫悅。
value.en: When the banquet ended, Yan summoned Yue to ride back with him to the Ministry of Justice, hoping to win him over.
value.literal: seats ended, Yan called Yue share carriage return to Ministry office, wished mutually to soothe and please.

value.zh: 瀹正色曰：「君巢窟在何處！」
value.en: Yue said with a stern face, "Where is your nest and den!"
value.literal: Yue stern countenance said: "my lord's nest den at what place!"

value.zh: 晏甚憚之。
value.en: Yan was deeply intimidated by him.
value.literal: Yan greatly feared him.
